82429.subject: Sky Moves to Halt New Borrowing on Legacy Vaults
82429.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

These are the biggest stories in DeFi and crypto:

* [**Sky**](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/sky-advisor-proposes-halting-new-core-vault-borrowing)[ may stop new borrowing on five legacy vaults](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/sky-advisor-proposes-halting-new-core-vault-borrowing)

* [**LlamaRisk**](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/llamarisk-proposes-borrowing-speed-limits-for-aave-v3)[ proposed borrowing speed limits for Aave](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/llamarisk-proposes-borrowing-speed-limits-for-aave-v3)

* [**Bitcoin**](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-breaks-below-72-000-as-multiweek-slide-deepens)[ fell below $72,000, and ether neared $2,000](https://thedefiant.io/news/markets/bitcoin-breaks-below-72-000-as-multiweek-slide-deepens)

* [**Binance**](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-says-hack-assets-covered-reserve-proof-pending)[ says hack losses are covered, proof pending](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/binance-says-hack-assets-covered-reserve-proof-pending)

* [**Tether**](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/usdt-freeze-proposals-on-tron-leave-time-to-move-funds)['s Tron freezes name targets before they execute](https://thedefiant.io/news/security/usdt-freeze-proposals-on-tron-leave-time-to-move-funds)

Three DeFi lenders moved this week to make new borrowing harder. Bitcoin fell below $72,000 on the same day the third proposal landed. What are the lenders are guarding against, and who pays for it?

**Sky**, formerly MakerDAO, issues the USDS and DAI stablecoins against collateral. On Thursday its risk advisor, BA Labs, [proposed stopping new borrowing](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/sky-advisor-proposes-halting-new-core-vault-borrowing) from five legacy ether and wstETH vault types. Those vaults hold 376.33 million USDS of debt across 771 positions. **Aave** is the largest DeFi lender, and LlamaRisk manages its risk settings. On Wednesday LlamaRisk [proposed a borrowing speed limit](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/llamarisk-proposes-borrowing-speed-limits-for-aave-v3) that refills a capped buffer every 30 minutes. **Moonwell**, a lender on Base and Optimism, [cut collateral limits](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/moonwell-cuts-collateral-limits-drops-velo-and-wrseth) the same day.

Moonwell, Binance and Aave each had an attack to deal with in the past four months. In August an attacker [took about $8.7 million from Moonwell](https://thedefiant.io/news/hacks/moonwell-loses-8-7-million-to-mamo-price-manipulation-on-base) by pushing up the price of MAMO and borrowing against it. Binance's October hack, which it puts at $6.3 billion, reached Aave next. A wallet in the attacker's cluster borrowed WETH on Aave, and LlamaRisk froze Aave markets across chains. Aave [reopened them on Oct. 30](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/aave-reopens-markets-but-keeps-nine-assets-at-zero-ltv) after removing about $3.7 billion of unused V3 borrowing capacity. 82420.subject: Are Quantum Computers a Threat to Bitcoin?
82420.body:
The Held Report

Автор: Dan Held


Автор: Dan Held

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/quantum-computers-threat-bitcoin-dan-held-wqave?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BLmWsCN%2F%2FTgaapcx%2B%2F4opeg%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=2D8hbwqhPbnIw1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mwdr4q2f~y7-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mwdr4q2f-y7
  
Hi everyone, Quantum computing is the most talked-about long-term threat to Bitcoin right now, and most of what you’re reading about it is either FUD or hand-waving. Below I’ve written out my classic long-form article, but if you’d rather watch a video, here is the video link. Below I’ll cover what quantum actually breaks, how many coins are exposed, how close the machines are, the two BIPs everyone is fighting about, and where I land. At the end there’s a 5-step checklist, including the one address type I’d stop using for long-term savings. Overview There are two main issues with upgrading Bitcoin to post-quantum: The upgrade itself: how to technically upgrade Bitcoin in time The old coins: what to do with coins that haven’t moved after the migration I’ve been in Bitcoin since 2012, and I’ve always looked at the protocol through its three core value props: the hardest monetary policy in history, an asset that’s extraordinarily difficult to seize, and a censorship-resistant ability to send money. Quantum computing is a real long-term risk to the second one. But it’s not the apocalyptic FUD some people portray. It’s a solvable engineering problem that needs calm, rational discussion now. What quantum breaks (and what it doesn’t) What it breaks: your wallet/private key. Shor’s algorithm on a big enough quantum computer turns a public key into a private key. What it doesn’t break: mining or the 21M cap. Adam Back put it simply: “quantum computers are NOT good at attacking hash functions. attacking bitcoin’s PoW is not the thing to focus on - it’s ECDSA.” (Aug 3, 2026) There are two kinds of attack: Long exposure (coins at rest): the public key is already on-chain, so the attacker has unlimited time. Short exposure (coins in transit): your public key sits in the mempool until it confirms, about 10 minutes on average. Long-exposure ones get hit first because a quantum computer can take all the time it needs to crack the keys. How much BTC is exposed? As of May 20, 2026, 6.04M BTC, or 30.2% of issued supply, has a visible public key. Other counts run higher: Project Eleven has ~6.8M BTC (Google’s paper cites ~6.9M) (Bitcoin Risq List). And the number that matters most for the Satoshi debate: Jameson Lopp estimates at least 2.6M BTC (about 13% of supply) would stay vulnerable even if every active user migrated to post-quantum secure cryptography (Bitcoin Magaz
